pageCache.text:
Welcome to Bousfield Primary School
We will always offer you the very warmest of welcomes at our happy and successful community school. We hope that you will find our website informative and helpful. Whether you are a prospective parent, somebody who might be interested in working at our school, or are already part of our school community, we hope that there is something here for you. Here at Bousfield, we aim to balance the highest academic aspirations for every single child with a rich offer of music, art, dance, sport and pastoral care.
We are fortunate to be based on a green and spacious site in the heart of Inner London, where children have the freedom to play, explore, and enjoy the outdoors every day. Our school-run Forest School gives pupils the chance to build confidence and resilience through hands-on experiences in nature, while our chickens, beehive, and allotment provide real-life opportunities to learn about care, responsibility, and food production. With the support of our outdoor kitchen, children can cook with the produce they have grown and even enjoy our own honey, making learning truly come to life. This unique environment enriches learning across the curriculum and helps our children develop a deep appreciation of the natural world.
We are ever grateful for the support we receive from our pupils past and present, our families, governors, staff and the wider community, who all help us in our vision to provide the most wonderful school experience for the children here. The school aims to work closely with parents.
Parents play a vital role in ensuring the success of Bousfield and are strongly encouraged to become involved in the life of the school. Regular newsletters are sent out to inform parents of key events and dates and to celebrate pupils' learning and achievements.
We are confident that you will see that Bousfield Primary School is a vibrant, dynamic and happy place. We are proud of our children, our staff and the provision we offer, and we look forward to welcoming you to our school so you can experience the warmth, energy and joy of our community for yourself.

pageCache.text:
Our Ethos & Values
The vision we hold is shared by all members of our community. The children and adults know that our motto and rules for growing embody everything we strive to accomplish.
We also teach our pupils about British Values through assemblies, PSHE and day to day life and routines in our school.
Similarly, teaching about equity, equality and inclusion is aided by ensuring protected characteristics are noted and explained to children in an appropriate way.

Special Education Needs & Disabilities
Our process
Your Concerns
We will be very happy to speak to you about any aspects of your child’s education. It is advisable to speak to one of the following in this order:
1 - Your child's class teacher
2 - The Special Education Needs Coordinator (SENCo) – Alice Boyd
3 - The Headteacher – Jane Griffiths
SEND Policy
Our policy aligns with the SEN Code of Practice which provides statutory guidance on the SEND system for children and young people aged 0 to 25.
Governing bodies of maintained schools and maintained nursery schools and the proprietors of academy schools must publish information on their websites about the implementation of the governing body’s or the proprietor’s policy for pupils with SEN. The information required is set out in the Special Educational Needs and Disability Regulations 2014.
Please find the school's latest policy and information report on our policies page.
Royal Borough of Kensington & Chelsea Local Offer
A 'local offer' gives children and young people with special educational needs and disabilities (SEND) and their families information to help them find the right help and support in their area.
RBKC's website has a wide range of information and services available to support you.
Sometimes it can be tricky to keep track of all the complex words and abbreviations used when talking about special educational needs and disabilities (SEND).
To make it a bit easier, the Bi-Borough (RBKC and Westminster) have produced a glossary of 'key words' explained to help you break down some of that technical language.
SEND Key Words Explained
Secondary School: Transition for SEN Children
Starting secondary school is a big step for every child, and for those with special educational needs or disabilities (SEND), it can be an even greater challenge. As a parent, you’ll want to make sure that the new school knows how to meet your child’s needs whether that is continuing in mainstream or moving to a specialist school. Some secondary schools will have specific units to support children with autism and continue with small group learning. We suggest starting to explore these options in Year 4. Please reach out to Alice Boyd, SENCo, to discuss further.

Sports Premium
The PE and School Sport Premium is part of a joint strategy supported and funded by the Department for Education (DfE), Department for Health (DfH) and the Department for Culture, Media and Sport (DCMS). The funding has been allocated to Primary Schools to “improve the quality and breadth of Physical Education and Sport Provision, including increasing participation so that all pupils develop healthy lifestyles and reach the performance levels they are capable of.” Schools have a duty to report on this premium annually to the DfE.
Sports Premium Impact Report 2024/5

Governing Body
Governors play a vital role in ensuring the best possible education for every child by creating robust accountability for school leaders.
The full Governing Body meets twice every term and operates as a flat structure, with no committees.
The Governing Body is comprised of 12 members and the composition is as follows

Learning in Nature
We are fortunate to be blessed with a large, green school site, and we make the most of it to enrich teaching and learning in every year group. We believe children learn best when they are connected to the natural world, and our grounds provide daily opportunities to explore, discover, and grow.
From the very start of school, pupils experience the changing seasons through Year 1’s dedicated “Season Weeks,” immersing themselves in the sights, sounds, and rhythms of nature. Our allotment and outdoor kitchen allow children to plant, harvest, and cook fresh produce, while our school chickens and bees give pupils the chance to take responsibility for caring for living things and to see first-hand the importance of sustainability.
This year marks the beginning of our Forest School journey. We are proud to have two classroom-based members of staff who have completed Forest School accreditation. They are working alongside teachers to support the planning of sessions and are developing a progressive scheme of work that will grow with the school. While still in its early stages, Forest School is already offering pupils valuable opportunities to explore, take risks, and learn new skills in a natural setting.
We also dedicate a full curriculum week each year to nature, sustainability, and global responsibility. Through outdoor projects, themed learning, and whole-school activities, pupils are encouraged to see themselves as global citizens and stewards of the planet.
Our outdoor learning is not an optional extra but a vital part of our curriculum. It nurtures curiosity, builds resilience, and develops creativity, while fostering a lifelong respect for the environment.

Maths
At Bousfield, we believe mathematics is not only a vital life skill but also a subject of beauty, creativity and wonder. Mathematics helps pupils make sense of the world, see patterns, and develop logical thinking that will serve them throughout their lives.
Our approach is rooted in mastery. Every child should develop a deep, secure understanding of mathematical concepts before moving on. Lessons balance three key elements, fluency, reasoning and problem solving, so that pupils can recall facts quickly, explain their thinking, and apply knowledge flexibly to new situations.
We place strong emphasis on fluency in number and arithmetic, as this provides the foundation for success in all areas of maths. Children are taught to use and recall their times tables with confidence, recognising them as essential tools for higher-level mathematical thinking.
To secure understanding, pupils are encouraged to use a wide range of manipulatives and visual representations. These practical resources, such as counters, cubes and number lines, help children grasp abstract concepts and bridge the gap between concrete experience and symbolic reasoning.
Reasoning is at the heart of our curriculum. Children are challenged to explain, justify and prove their ideas, as well as to make connections across different areas of mathematics. Problem solving opportunities are woven through lessons so that pupils learn to apply their skills in meaningful, often real-life, contexts.
Throughout, we celebrate the beauty and wonder of mathematics, from the elegance of patterns in nature to the creativity of exploring multiple solutions. We want our pupils to see maths not only as a tool for success but also as a subject to enjoy and take pride in.
Our ultimate aim is that every child leaves Bousfield as a confident, fluent and flexible mathematician, equipped to thrive in the next stage of their education and to approach the world with curiosity and critical thinking.

Music
At Bousfield, music is given high priority. We are delighted to have been awarded the Music Mark of Recognition for Dedication & Improvement, recognising the value we place on music and our continued commitment to strengthening musical opportunities for every child at Bousfield. Music is an important part of life at our school, both within the curriculum and through the many opportunities children have to perform, create, learn an instrument and make music together. We are particularly proud that our work has been recognised by the Tri-borough Music Hub and Music Mark, the UK Association for Music Education. This recognition reflects the hard work of our staff, the enthusiasm of our pupils and our belief that a rich musical education should be part of every child’s experience at Bousfield.
Every pupil has the chance to explore a wide range of sounds, styles, and instruments. EYFS children receive 30 minutes of weekly music including nursery rhymes, percussion, singing, and drama. Pupils in Key Stages 1 and 2 have at least one hour of music each week, supported by whole-class instrumental lessons using Groove and Play, and weekly singing assemblies feature a Music of the Week to introduce different styles, composers, and cultures.
Children can learn guitar, cello, violin, or piano through peripatetic lessons, along with a music theory club with places funded for pupil premium pupils. Children can take also part in our free school choir, string ensemble, and free drumming club. Partnerships with organisations such as Odyssey Festival Orchestra provide workshops and performance opportunities, and we publicise other external opportunities, including Holland Park Youth Chorus.
Throughout the year, pupils perform in assemblies, termly concerts, the spring concert, and winter and summer plays, and they also enjoy live professional performances. All events are inclusive and subsidised where needed, giving every child the chance to sing, play, and enjoy music, developing confidence, creativity, and a lifelong love of music.

Science
At Bousfield, science is an exciting, hands-on journey of discovery that helps pupils explore the world around them. We aim to inspire curiosity, develop investigative skills, and foster a deep understanding of scientific concepts across biology, chemistry and physics.
Our lessons are practical and enquiry-based, giving children the opportunity to observe, test and experiment. Pupils are encouraged to ask questions, make predictions, and draw conclusions, developing the critical thinking and problem-solving skills that underpin scientific understanding.
Science at Bousfield is closely linked to the world outside the classroom. Our Forest School, school allotment and beehives provide rich, real-life contexts for learning. Children explore plants, animals and ecosystems, study growth and life cycles, and witness science in action, making learning tangible, memorable and meaningful.
We emphasise the importance of scientific vocabulary, reasoning and explanation, ensuring that children can communicate their ideas clearly and accurately. Practical investigations are combined with opportunities to record findings, interpret data and make connections across different areas of science.
Through all of this, we celebrate the wonder and fascination of science, from the patterns in nature to the marvels of the universe. We want our pupils to see science as a subject to enjoy, explore and take pride in, building confidence to ask questions and seek answers throughout their lives.
Our ultimate aim is that every child leaves Bousfield as a curious, knowledgeable and confident young scientist, equipped to continue their learning journey and engage with the natural and technological world with understanding and awe.

Curriculum
At Bousfield, our curriculum is broad, rich, and carefully planned to inspire curiosity, creativity, and a love of learning. It equips children with the knowledge and skills they need to succeed, while also giving them opportunities to explore, question, and make connections across subjects.
Each subject has its own clear intent and progression, creating a joined-up journey from the early years to Year 6. Our curriculum is further enriched through trips, visitors, and hands-on experiences that bring learning to life and reflect the diversity of our community.
The school uses Google Classroom for some aspects of homework and in the event of school closure due to weather or national emergency, Google Classroom will be used for access to remote learning.
Use the side tabs to find out more about each subject area.
If you wish to find out anything further about our curriculum, please contact Mrs Griffiths, the headteacher.

Art & Design
At Bousfield, Art is a vibrant and integral part of our curriculum. Our pupils develop skills, creativity and confidence year by year, producing work of a standard that consistently impresses visitors. Many of our children’s pieces have been showcased beyond the classroom, including in the Royal Academy Summer Exhibition, demonstrating the high level of talent nurtured at the school.
Art is woven throughout our curriculum, both in dedicated lessons and during annual curriculum weeks, ensuring that every child has the opportunity to explore a wide range of media, techniques and artistic ideas. Every September, we create a communal piece of art as a whole school, celebrating community, togetherness and the start of the academic year. Our school also hosts an art exhibition open to the public every other year, giving children the pride and experience of displaying their work for a wider audience.
In lessons, pupils learn about influential artists and study their techniques, styles and approaches. Art is celebrated in our assemblies as well, with an “Art of the Week” feature that highlights art history and sparks inspiration across the school.
Through creating and studying art, children develop not only technical skills but also creativity, critical thinking and self-expression. Our aim is that every child leaves Bousfield with a strong artistic foundation, a love of creativity, and the confidence to continue exploring art throughout their lives.

Computing
At Bousfield, Computing equips children with the knowledge, skills and confidence to thrive in an increasingly digital world. From Reception onwards, pupils benefit from weekly lessons in our dedicated computer suite, where they develop their understanding of technology through hands-on learning. In addition, Chromebooks and tablets are used across the curriculum where technology can enhance learning and support children in achieving their best. We also recognise the important role technology can play in promoting inclusion, using appropriate digital tools to help pupils access learning and develop independence.
Our Computing curriculum is informed by nationally recognised expertise and research in computing education and provides a carefully sequenced progression of knowledge and skills from the Early Years through to Year 6. Children learn about programming, data and digital media, creating a wide range of projects including animations, photography, audio recordings, videos, websites and three-dimensional designs. As they move through the school, pupils explore increasingly sophisticated technologies and develop the logical thinking, creativity and problem-solving skills that underpin successful computing.
Computing Curriculum Map
We recognise that helping children navigate the online world safely is one of the most important aspects of modern education. Online safety is taught throughout the school and woven through our Computing curriculum, helping children to understand topics such as privacy, digital footprints, responsible communication and respectful online behaviour. We work closely with parents to encourage safe and positive use of technology both at school and at home.
Technology continues to evolve at a rapid pace, and we regularly review and refine our curriculum to ensure that children develop the knowledge and skills they need for the future. Our aim is that every child leaves Bousfield as a confident, responsible and discerning user of technology, prepared for the opportunities and challenges of the digital world.

English
At Bousfield, English sits at the heart of our curriculum because strong communication skills open doors to every other area of learning. Through reading, writing, speaking and listening, pupils learn to express themselves with clarity, imagination and confidence.
English Curriculum Map
From the very beginning of school, we prioritise reading. Phonics is taught systematically using the Essential Letters and Sounds scheme, ensuring that every child builds secure foundations for fluent and accurate reading. This structured approach enables children to decode confidently and make rapid progress. Alongside phonics, we place a strong emphasis on developing comprehension and vocabulary so that pupils can not only read words but also understand, enjoy and discuss them.
At Bousfield, we believe passionately in the love of reading. Children are immersed in a wide range of high-quality texts, from timeless classics to contemporary works that reflect diverse voices and perspectives. Reading for pleasure is central to our approach: classrooms are full of rich book corners, we host regular reading events, and we encourage children to see books as both a source of knowledge and a gateway to imagination.
In writing, pupils develop accuracy, creativity and stamina. They are taught to craft their ideas through modelling, shared writing, and editing, ensuring they can write effectively for a range of audiences and purposes. Grammar, punctuation and spelling are embedded within meaningful contexts, supporting children to become precise and confident writers.
Oracy underpins everything we do: pupils are encouraged to articulate their thinking, listen attentively, and engage respectfully in discussion and debate. Drama is also a longstanding tradition at Bousfield, with our amphitheatre and two halls providing inspiring spaces for performance. These opportunities allow children to bring texts to life, build confidence in public speaking, and experience the joy of performing for an audience.
We are committed to ensuring that every child succeeds in English, including those with additional needs. Support is carefully tailored, and we use a range of strategies to ensure access and progress for all learners. In particular, the Lexia programme provides targeted, personalised support to help children develop reading skills with confidence.
Our ultimate aim is that every child leaves Bousfield as an enthusiastic reader, a capable writer, and a confident communicator, fully prepared for the next stage of their education.

Geography
At Bousfield, Geography helps children develop an understanding of the world around them, from our local community to countries, cultures and environments across the globe. As a school with families from a wide range of nationalities and backgrounds, Geography provides valuable opportunities for children to share experiences, explore different perspectives and learn about the diverse world in which we live.
A particular strength of Geography at Bousfield is our Map Mastery programme. Throughout the school, children develop increasingly sophisticated map-reading skills using aerial photographs, atlases, Ordnance Survey maps and digital resources. These skills are revisited and built upon year by year, helping pupils become confident and capable geographers.
Our local area provides a rich starting point for geographical learning. Through fieldwork, map work and first-hand observation, children explore the neighbourhood around the school before broadening their understanding to topics such as rivers, rainforests, climate, natural disasters and global trade. Geography is also celebrated through our curriculum weeks, including Blue Planet Week, where pupils explored oceans, rivers and seas through a range of engaging activities.
We are proud of a curriculum that reflects both the diversity of our school community and the wider world. Through Geography, children develop curiosity, respect and environmental responsibility. Our aim is that every child leaves Bousfield with strong geographical knowledge, confident map-reading skills and a lifelong interest in the people, places and environments that shape our planet.
